task: Harden /api/transcribe against a real ECONNRESET suspect and stop swallowing error causes: drop the pointless `stream: true` (this route only ever sent one JSON response, so streaming bought nothing but a long-lived SSE connection to OpenAI -- the leading suspect for the incident), and return a redacted `detail` from both /api/transcribe and /api/summarize error responses. Paired with a new stated-level channel so a driver can tell runtime.js the severity of its own status directly instead of only through prose classification.

server.js.summary: Removed `stream: true` from the OpenAI transcriptions.create call and the for-await delta/done accumulation loop that only ever fed one res.json() reply -- the route never streamed anything to its own client, so the SSE connection was pure downside (a long-lived stream on a flaky path is the leading suspect for an unreproduced ECONNRESET). Reads transcription.text directly instead. Added safeErrorDetail(error): extracts a short (MAX_ERROR_DETAIL_LENGTH 200 chars) detail from a caught error's code/cause.code/message, redacting anything matching API_KEY_PATTERN (sk-... / sk-ant-...) or AUTH_HEADER_PATTERN (Authorization: ...) so INV-12 (provider keys never leave the server) holds for error text too, not just the key store. Both the /api/transcribe and /api/summarize catch blocks now return { error, detail: safeErrorDetail(error) } instead of a bare error string.

public/controller/runtime.js.summary: buildTranscriptionDriver's onStatus callback now accepts an optional second argument { level } from the driver and prefers statedLevel over transcriptionStatusLevel(text) when present, falling back to the prose classifier only when the driver doesn't state one -- because sniffing wording was the only channel until now and silently misses any message phrased outside its regex.

public/services/transcription/openai.js.summary: First caller of the stated-level channel: the audio-shedding message ('Falling behind live speech...') is emitted via onStatus(text, { level: 'problem' }) rather than relying on runtime.js's classifier to recognise it, since dropping captured speech is serious but phrased in wording the classifier's regex does not match.

test/server/app.test.js.summary: Tests updated for the non-streaming transcription call and asserting the redacted `detail` field on transcribe/summarize error responses, including that a key-shaped or Authorization-shaped string never reaches the client.

test/public/controller/runtime.test.js.summary: Test asserting a driver-stated level is believed over the prose classifier even when the message wording wouldn't otherwise be classified as a problem.

flow_impact: Removes a suspected source of connection instability from the transcribe request path and closes a leak surface in both AI-backed routes' error responses; the new stated-level channel is additive to the existing driver onStatus -> updateStatus -> rail flow, letting a driver bypass prose classification when it already knows the severity.
